chunks: 1832 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: When the month of Ramadan approached, and that was with three days remaining of Sha‘ban, he said to Bilal, “Call out among the people.” So he gathered the people, then he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah, and extolled Him, then said:
"O people, this month has come upon you, and it is the master of the months. In it is a night which is

In it the gates of the Fire are closed, and in it the gates of the gardens are opened. So whoever reaches it and is not forgiven, then may Allah distance him. And whoever reaches his parents and is not forgiven, then may Allah distance him. And whoever I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me, and he is not forgiven, then may Allah distance him."

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ النَّارِ: The gates of the Fire, described here as being closed in Ramadan
key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الْجِنَانِ: The gates of the gardens of Paradise, described here as being opened in Ramadan
key_terms.خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ: A Qur'anic description of the night in Ramadan whose worship surpasses a thousand months
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The blessed month of fasting whose arrival the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله announces
key_terms.سَيِّدُ الشُّهُورِ: The master of the months, indicating Ramadan’s superiority
key_terms.وَالِدَيْهِ: One’s parents, whose presence is tied here to an opportunity for forgiveness
key_terms.يُصَلِّ عَلَيَّ: To send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله when he is mentioned

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the virtues of Ramadan and the importance of seeking forgiveness?
ai.summary: This hadith is a prophetic exhortation announcing the arrival and immense virtue of the month of Ramadan. It highlights Laylat al-Qadr, the opening of the gates of Paradise and closing of the gates of the Fire, and warns against failing to attain forgiveness in Ramadan, through dutifulness to one's parents, and by sending blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.
